$comment: A prompt call: the prompt of one stage, written from the texts the host fetched for it, by the kinds runAgent names. `texts` is the absolute path, POSIX or Windows, of the folder outside the working tree where the host keeps the whole texts a prompt shortens, which the agent reads; null when it reads no files. With `unfit`, why a session's result did not fit its schema, the answer is the prompt that asks the same session for its result alone. `words` are the host's own words for the work item, the change and where people read, which a stage's prompt needs. Beside the host's policies, `checklist`, `profiles` and `noChange` feed the prompts. The host also describes the evidence it fetched in its own words (`evidence`).

state.$comment: The fix and review prompts read the earlier fix rounds from `rounds.fixes`, the last review from `rounds.lastReview` and the change's current version from `change.version`; a request without a state, or whose state holds none of them, shows no earlier rounds. The newest fix record is the round a review follows.

policies.$comment: The host's policies, as every call has them, and three that only the prompts read: `checklist`, the items the plan and the review answer, `noChange`, the host's findings that show a plan or implement stage no change is needed (one to five, each a text whose line breaks the engine keeps and whose bullet it writes; the engine refuses a plan or implement call without them), and `profiles`, the profiles triage chooses from, each name with an object whose `when` is a string. A plan needs `budgets.implement.seconds` as an integer, the implement stage's time, which its prompt names; the engine refuses a plan without it, and a profile without a string `when`.

number.$comment: An id as the host shows it to people, such as a number.

inputs.$comment: The texts the host fetched, by the kinds that runAgent names (protocol.stages.INPUTS). Every stage needs `item`; implement, fix and review need `plan`, which may be null; fix and review need `diff`; every stage but triage needs `workspace`. A kind left out is empty.

notes.$comment: The note of the request that started the stage, "" without one.

plan.$comment: The approved plan, null without one.

item.$comment: The work item: its text, its change when it has one, and what the change did outside the plan.

person.$comment: A change a person made, reviewed as its own work item, with no plan.

outsidePlan.$comment: What the implement round did outside the plan, as it wrote it.

entry.$comment: One entry of a discussion, oldest first. The host leaves out what nobody it trusts wrote, and commands without a note.

kind.$comment: A person's comment, a note on a command, which only some stages read, or the answers a policy gave for the people who decide.

discussion.$comment: The discussion on the work item and on its change, and what people said on the change's version.

previousPlan.$comment: The latest plan, which a new plan revises.

before.$comment: How many entries of the item's discussion came before it.

profile.$comment: The profile it used, which triage reads.

check.$comment: A check's result with the end of its output and earlier lines that report a failure.

output.$comment: The end of its output, at most the last 12000 characters.

skipped.$comment: The version it passed on, when it did not run again.

required.$comment: A required check of the host's CI that failed, so the accept was refused. `refused` is why it was refused, the end of the heading "Required check `name` failed, so …", and `about` says what the check is, in the host's words, both outside the `<untrusted>` tags; the engine refuses a check without them.

checks.$comment: The results of the checks: in a fix round the last recorded, in a review this round's. `diagnose` holds the checks a diagnosis round looks into.

said.$comment: What a person said on the change's version: a review with its state, or a comment on a line.

linkedText.$comment: A text the item links to: a comment, the engine's plan, or the text of an item or a change.

above.$comment: An item a part was split from.

body.$comment: Null when the host did not read its text.

linked.$comment: What the item refers to and the agent cannot open itself.

chain.$comment: The items the item was split from, nearest first.

notRead.$comment: Each link the host did not read, and why, in its words; the host bounds how many it lists.

since.$comment: The host's words on whether a newer run of the same kind passed since, shown as the run's Since line; left out when it has none.

ciEvidence.$comment: What the runs the item names left, downloaded outside the working tree, in the host's own description: `name` is what the heading calls them ("the CI runs" becomes "Evidence from the CI runs this issue names"), and `about` is a paragraph, outside the `<untrusted>` tags, that says where the files are and what they hold. The engine writes no word about the evidence's kind.

name.$comment: What the heading calls the evidence, such as "the CI runs".

about.$comment: The host's paragraph on where the files are and what they hold.

keeps.$comment: The most bytes a round keeps of the runs.

resultsEvidence.$comment: The result files the failing checks kept, downloaded outside the working tree. `limit` is the host's sentence on how much its checks keep of them, shown after the number of files left out.

parts.$comment: The earlier parts of the same split that a part relies on, oldest first.

diff.$comment: The change, from the host's workspace. `merging` is the version of the base a fix round merges in and the files it conflicts in. `merged` is the merge of the base that the newest fix record in `state.rounds.fixes` made, the round a review follows.

base.$comment: What the change goes onto, such as a branch.

text.$comment: The change against its base. At most 80001 characters: the prompt shows 80000 and says so when there are more, so the host sends no more.

since.$comment: The change since the version the last review read; null when the host cannot show it. At most 80001 characters: the prompt shows 80000 and says so when there are more, so the host sends no more.

sides.$comment: In the files a merge of the base in this run's fix round conflicted in: the base's changes, then the change's, each at most 20001 characters; null when the host cannot show them.

head.$comment: The version the round started from.

base.$comment: The version of the base it merged in.

workspace.$comment: What the agent's workspace gives it: the checks it can run, the paths only a person changes and the host's own sentences on how the agent sees and edits the change, as `text`.

protected.$comment: The host's text for what only a person changes, one string for each, which the engine keeps without reading it.

workspaceText.$comment: The host's own sentences on how the agent sees and edits the change, which the plan, implement, fix and review prompts, and the sections of a review about a merge of the base and the round before, use in place of any host's. Each is a string of at most 500 characters and every field is required, in every call with a `workspace`, as the host's own text outside the `<untrusted>` tags: a host builds them only from its own fixed text, never from what people wrote. Each replaces one span of a prompt's line, so none holds a line break, except `mergeRule` and `sideHistory`, whose one sentence a template wraps over two lines. The engine refuses a `workspace` without `text`, or without one of its fields, and names the missing field.

location.$comment: Where the agent works, as the end of "You are the planning agent, ...", such as "working through the application's tools on request R-12".

reviewLocation.$comment: A sentence on what the review sees, such as "The review sees draft 3 as it is now.".

candidate.$comment: The version of the change that the checks ran on and the review sees, such as "the candidate draft".

instructions.$comment: Where the host keeps the project's instructions, in parentheses after "conventions and instructions", such as "(the application's style notes)".

saving.$comment: The rule on how the agent's edits are kept, a whole sentence, such as "Do not publish the draft. The application saves your edits.".

leftovers.$comment: The rule on what the agent leaves behind, a whole sentence, such as "Leave no scratch records in the draft.".

summaryUse.$comment: What the agent's summary becomes, such as "the draft's note".

checksOn.$comment: Where the checks ran, after "Project checks," in a heading, such as "run on this exact draft".

diffHeading.$comment: The heading of the change's diff, before the base, such as "Changes against".

pipeline.$comment: What runs the checks, as the review limits name it, such as "the application's validation rules".

pipelineFiles.$comment: The plural of what a person's change to the pipeline may touch, such as "validation rules".

pipelineFile.$comment: One of them with its article, such as "a validation rule".

protectedExample.$comment: An example of a protected path, with its code marks, such as "`settings/limits`".

personChange.$comment: Where a person's change is, after "changes nothing", such as "in this draft".

fixLocation.$comment: Where the fix agent works, as the end of the fix prompt's first line before the change's name, such as "working through the application's tools on".

earlierWork.$comment: A whole sentence that says the change already holds earlier work, such as "The draft already holds earlier edits.".

mergeRule.$comment: The rule against merging by hand, a whole sentence, such as "Do not take in the published request yourself. The application does that when the round needs it.". It may hold line breaks, and indents its own further lines by two spaces as a bullet's continuation.

versionKind.$comment: The noun for one version of the change, which the merge and previous-review sections use before an id, such as "version".

baseKind.$comment: The noun for what the change is merged with, after "the", such as "published request".

mergeInto.$comment: Where the base was merged and in what state, after the base and its version, such as "into the draft, without saving it".

lastMerged.$comment: When the base last reached the change, after "has moved since", such as "this draft last took it in".

mergeUndo.$comment: How the agent leaves a merge in place, after "Leave the merge in place:", a whole clause that ends with a full stop, such as "do not discard or publish it.".

sideHistory.$comment: A sentence on how the agent sees what each side changed in a conflicted file, such as "The draft's history shows what each side changed.". It may hold line breaks, and indents its own further lines by two spaces as a bullet's continuation.

sideNote.$comment: A sentence that says a note one side left is no answer to a conflict, such as "A side's note is not an answer.".

otherVersions.$comment: A sentence for the review after no fix round, such as "Any later versions were saved without a fix round.".

workspaceName.$comment: Where the agent reads the change, in the engine's notes that a version or a diff is not there, such as "this draft's history".

locationForm.$comment: How the agent writes where a review finding points, after "`location` is", such as "the record and its field, such as `form Customer › field Phone`, or an empty string when it is about no record". The engine keeps what the agent writes, clipped, and shows it to the next fix and review prompts without reading it.

words.$comment: The host's words, as its people see them, which the prompts of the stages use in place of any host's own. Each is a string of at most 200 characters, and every field is required, as the host's own text and outside the `<untrusted>` tags: a host builds them only from its own fixed text and ids, never from what people wrote. `itemKind` and `changeKind` are nouns the prompts use in rules, such as "the request's scope"; `itemKinds` is the plural, which cannot be made from the noun. A template breaks a line inside `item` and `changeKind`, which the engine does at their last space. The engine refuses a stage's prompt without `words` and names the missing field; a call with `unfit` needs none.

item.$comment: The work item in a sentence, with its id, such as "request R-42".

itemHeading.$comment: The work item as the heading of its text, such as "Request R-42".

itemKind.$comment: The noun for a work item, such as "request".

change.$comment: The work item's change with its id, such as "draft 3"; "" when the item has none.

changeKind.$comment: The noun for a change, such as "draft".

source.$comment: Where people wrote the texts the prompt shows, such as "in the app".

readers.$comment: Where people read the agent's text, such as "in the app".

approve.$comment: The words that approve a plan, such as "*Approve*".

fixRound.$comment: The words that ask for a fix round, such as "*Fix*".

commands.$comment: The commands people write on the item, with their noun, such as "the app's actions".
